title: Michigan Man Pleads Guilty in String of Bank and Credit Union Robberies Terrorizing Detroit - NewsBreak
text:
4 hours ago DETROIT – A Detroit man has admitted to a series of bank and credit union robberies, federal officials announced Wednesday. Dorian Trevor Sykes, 42, of Detroit, pleaded guilty to four counts of robbery and one count of attempted robbery, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Michigan.
Photo by Dmytro Demidko on Unsplash United States Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon made the announcement alongside Reuben C. Coleman, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Detroit Field Division. Authorities said Sykes carried out the crimes over a one-week period in March 2025.
According to court documents, between March 6 and March 12, 2025, Sykes robbed two credit unions and one bank, stealing more than $20,000. He also attempted to rob another bank during the spree. In the last two incidents, prosecutors said, Sykes drove a rented luxury vehicle that cost more than $1,000 a day. He later used the same car to lead police on a high-speed chase through the Detroit area.
Sentencing is scheduled for March 17, 2026. Each count of bank or credit union robbery, as well as attempted robbery, carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison, a $250,000 fine, or both, according to federal officials.
The FBI’s Macomb County Gang and Violent Crime Task Force led the investigation, with support from the Sterling Heights Police Department, Livonia Police Department, Redford Township Police Department, and Lathrup Village Police Department. The case is being prosecuted by the Violent and Major Crimes Unit of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Michigan.
